title: The spare panty liner in the handbag

format_analysis.format: V1: problem-object hook + impersonal brand voiceover over fast, faceless b-roll. An object-cam POV (the camera inside her handbag) opens on the spare panty liner the instant after a sneeze. A warm, wry narrator then roasts that liner's day over locked macro hand shots. Plain black underwear is revealed, pulled on under leggings, and she gets on with an errand. The ad hands a qualified click to the quiz.
format_analysis.how_it_should_look: Real-UGC phone look, not cinematic: iPhone 4K with natural phone sharpening and light grain, honest and bright, never dark or clinical. The hook and car-park shots feel handheld; the roast is tripod-locked macro (phone macro mode, 10-15cm) with ONE tiny hand action per VO word. Palette: tan leather, cream/blush bedding and tiles, pastel liner wrappers, and one hard black object (the underwear). The black is the only dense dark thing in the ad, so the 8.5s flash and the 11s reveal pop. Grade warm (+5 temp) with lifted interiors; keep the liner pure white (no yellow cast). Captions: Hanken Grotesk ExtraBold, Plum Ink on Warm Cream boxes, one phrase at a time in the 14-62% band inside the 4:5 crop; hook line 1 in a Claret pill with cream text; Fraunces only on the end-card brand line. Sound: a wry, light, plucked music bed (Meta Sound Collection or licensed) ducked under the VO, with a lift at 11.0s, an SFX on every cut in 0-10s and a chime on the button. VO: a warm, wry woman in her 30s, brisk staccato at ~3 words/sec (the refs' measured pace).
format_analysis.build_profile: HOOK 0-3s: faceless, hands only (her chin/shoulder at most a blur), an off-screen ACHOO SFX + brand VO. BODY 3-11s: faceless macro hand shots, brand VO. REVEAL 11-17s: product in hands, then a headless side-on body (waist-to-knee, getting dressed). 17-25s: a full-figure woman in leggings in the car park, face never featured, no dialogue. CTA/END: product plate + editor cards. Voice path: ONE ElevenLabs brand narrator, recorded first, with the pictures cut to it. No on-camera speech, so no lip-sync anywhere.

reference_ads.what_we_take: UltraDries video #6 (193d). Its hook throws the object AT the lens and holds ~3.0s with a boxed caption mid-frame from frame 0; after that, EVERY cut is a new place or subject (8 cuts in 3-10s). We copy that cut density and the 'never the same room twice in a row' rule in the roast (bed > bathroom > gym bag > bin > flash > hallway > in-bag). Its VO also names our exact pain at 39.5s ('Carrying pads in your purse everywhere you go'), which is in-category proof that the spare-in-the-bag moment lands.

Everdries video #14 (275d, 6 dupes). It opens on a POV down at the problem object, with the contrarian 'still using pads?' text on screen from frame 0, held 3.4s, and an emoji popping in at ~1.5s (our 🙄 on line 2). Then hands-on-bed b-roll where every shot has motion in it (flip, point, unwrap), which becomes our locked macros with a micro-action on each VO word. Its on-body waistband pull at ~21s maps to our leggings pull-up. We do NOT copy its stained pad (no stains) or its 'you'.
Miro #75 Fridge POV example (Dukes Health, 165d): the camera lives where the product lives, and a hand reaches in and takes it. That is the mechanic of our handbag-cam.
Anti-pattern only: a hand demo held as one 18-41s take. Our roast never holds a frame longer than 1.35s.

recommended.text: Sneeze. Little pee. / Still packing a spare panty liner? 🙄
recommended.on_screen_timing: Line 1 is on screen from 0.00 to 3.00s (on frame 0, popping in over 4 frames). Line 2 stacks UNDER line 1 at 1.30s (it does not replace it) and holds to 3.00s, carried across the 2.20s hand-wipe. The 🙄 pops onto the end of line 2 at ~1.90s.
recommended.style: Line 1: Claret #A33154 pill, Warm Cream #F5EDE6 text, Hanken Grotesk ExtraBold, cap height ~5.5% of frame height, centred ~18% from the top. Line 2: Warm Cream box, Plum Ink #231017 text, Hanken Grotesk ExtraBold ~4.2% height, directly below (~25% from the top), max 2 lines. Both sit inside the centre 4:5 crop and ABOVE the liner (never over it), which sits in the 30-62% band.
recommended.why: Keep the locked words: it is the best stopper for THIS visual. Line 1 is 3 words, so it reads in under 0.5s, names the moment and the word 'pee' sound-off on frame 0, is undated, and has no 'you' (passes Meta's personal-attributes rule). The handbag POV + jolt does the physical stopping. Line 2 imports the proven 'still using [the old workaround]?' contrarian from Everdries' 275d 'It's 2025! Why are you still using pads? 🤢' (6 dupes, video #14), minus the date and minus the 'you'. Its one weakness is that line 1 is a flat statement with no tension, so the fixes are presentation only: STACK the lines (Everdries holds one two-line card for 3.4s; ours shouldn't make her read two separate cards in 3s), put the stopper line in the Claret pill, and add the eye-roll pop that Everdries uses as an in-hook motion event (🙄 = the wry 'same routine' emotion; 🤢 would read as a hygiene cue on a clean liner).

alternates.text: It's 2026! / Still packing a panty liner for a sneeze? 🙄
alternates.why: The literal copy of the proven contrarian structure (year stamp + 'still' + the old workaround + emoji pop at ~1.5s), with no 'you' and the moment named in line 2. Best A/B challenger. Costs: it's dated (swap to 2027 in January, the landmine Nikita already removed), 'pee' leaves the screen, and line 2 is 8 words (~1.5s to read).
alternates.proven_anchor: "It's 2025! Why are you still using pads? 🤢" - Everdries 1206351388295667, 275 days live, 6 dupes, video #14

alternates.text: Sneezing shouldn't require a spare panty liner.
alternates.why: Six words. A normative contrarian aimed at the routine, not at her, with no 'you'. It implies the underwear replaces the liner on a sneeze, so it can run only once the founder wear test logs the sneeze (that gate is campaign-wide anyway).
alternates.proven_anchor: "Sneezing shouldn't require crossing your legs." - clinic caption, Advanced Health 1015538471405847, 112 days live (AD_RESEARCH §3: passes Meta as written; Tier B, caption-only)

alternates.text: For anyone who packs a spare panty liner for sneezes 🙄
alternates.why: The same moment and object, addressed to the habit in the third person, never to a condition, so it's Meta-safe. 9 words, so it reads slower than the recommended line. Use it if Meta flags the question form.
alternates.proven_anchor: "Leak when you sneeze?" - Origin, 372 days live (the longest-running 30-45 hook), via AD_RESEARCH §3's sanctioned third-person rewrite "For anyone who's crossed her legs before a sneeze."

text_hook.note: The recommended hook keeps the locked words plus the word-rule swap ('liner' > 'panty liner'). It differs from the script only in presentation: the lines stack instead of replacing each other, line 1 sits in the Claret hook pill instead of the script's cream box, and a 🙄 pops on line 2. The VO line 2 is also trimmed (see vo_fit_issues). Nikita chiefs it.

visual_hook_build.frame_1: Inside an open tan leather zip-top tote on her lap in a parked car. One clean white panty liner in a long, flat, pale-pink, unbranded wrapper (pull-tab visible) fills ~40-45% of the frame, dead-centre in the 30-62% band, tilted ~25 deg and pin-sharp. Behind it, out of focus: a plain key ring and a phone lying screen-down in a plain case, both dark, and nothing else. Above, the bag mouth is a bright oval of overcast daylight from the open driver door; at most a soft blur of her chin/shoulder at the top edge. The Claret pill 'Sneeze. Little pee.' is popping in at ~18% from the top. Bright, sharp, and readable as 'a panty liner in a handbag' in one glance.
build_steps: COMPARE AND PICK: real phone in a real bag (owned-phone) vs AI start frame + motion. RECOMMEND OWNED-PHONE. It gives real relative physics (keys slide, the liner hops, light flares as the hand clears the mouth), a real hand-on-object grab (the hardest thing for video models), the true phone-grain UGC look the UltraDries #6 winner runs on, zero credits and zero AI drift. It is NOT blocked on CJ samples (there's no product in the hook), and the same rig also shoots S10's zip-close callback. Its only requirement is a woman's hand. AI is the fallback (see fallback).

PROPS: a tan/caramel leather ZIP-TOP tote with a wide mouth, a plain cream/beige lining and no logo plaque. A pack of long flat-pack panty liners in pale pink/lilac wrappers with no print (or the print turned down / covered with matte pastel washi tape). Plain house keys (no car-brand fob). A prop phone in a plain case, screen-down (hide the Apple logo). A rolled hand towel, a cardboard wedge and gaffer tape. Do NOT add tissues, receipts or lip balm: no other white or pastel item may compete with the liner.

RIG: tape the shooting phone (4K 60fps, 0.5x ultra-wide or macro mode, Action mode OFF, Cinematic OFF) to the cardboard wedge, lens up at ~45 deg, and wedge it in the rolled towel at the bottom of the bag so it can't tip during the jolt. The screen faces the bag wall. Hit record before placing it.

KEEP THE LINER READING AS A LINER, NOT CLUTTER: use the long flat liner shape (an elongated wrapper with a pull-tab reads 'liner'; a folded square packet reads as a wet wipe, condom or sweet). Lay it on top of everything, 10-12cm from the lens, centred, long axis at ~25 deg, tab toward the mouth, in the sharp plane. Keep exactly two other items, both dark and 25-30cm back, so they go to bokeh. It must be the only light pastel object in frame, with pale pink on tan leather for tone contrast. The text sits ABOVE it, never on it. S2 then confirms it in daylight: her thumb pops the tab and the white liner edge shows, and line 2 names it 'panty liner'. Check playback: the liner must be >=40% of the frame and sharp on frame 0.

LIGHT: parked car, overcast day, driver door open, bag on her lap tilted toward the door so daylight pours into the mouth. Long-press AE/AF lock on the liner, expose for it and let the sky bloom (that's the 'light floods in' look). If the interior is murky, add a white card on her lap or a small LED cube taped inside below the frame. Frame 0 must never be dark.

THE SNEEZE JOLT, IN-CAMERA (primary): on her cue she does a sharp sneeze-jerk (shoulders forward, knees pop up ~3-5cm), so the bag on her lap drops and bounces. Because the phone is wedged tight, the frame stays on the liner while the loose keys and liner shift RELATIVE to the camera and the daylight in the mouth jumps; that relative movement is what sells it. She can say 'achoo' for timing, and it gets replaced by the SFX. Keep Action mode OFF or it irons the jolt flat.

THE SNEEZE JOLT, EDITOR (accent only): CapCut keyframes on the ACHOO transient at 0.10s, 3-5 frames: scale 100>107>100%, position +/-12px, rotation +/-1.5 deg, plus a 2-frame directional blur and the key-jangle SFX. Never use an editor-only shake: a rigid whole-frame wobble with nothing moving inside the bag reads fake.

ACTION (8-12 takes, ~4s each): jolt, then ~0.5s later her right hand (short natural nails, thin gold band, no other jewellery) dives in from the top of the mouth straight at the lens and pinches the liner by its tab. The liner must stay >=60% visible until ~1.2s. She yanks it up and out toward the light and, on the exit, sweeps the BACK of her hand across the lens (the dark wipe used for the hidden cut).

S2 IN THE SAME SESSION: she holds the phone at chest height facing the windscreen (steering-wheel badge taped or out of frame), starts with the back of her hand covering the lens, pulls back to reveal the liner 20cm out, and flicks the tab half-open. S10 IN THE SAME RIG on the hallway table: drop in a fresh liner, then zip the mouth shut across the lens.

EDIT: start the clip 3 frames before the jolt (frame 0 = sharp liner + pill popping). Join S1 to S2 inside the hand-wipe. Grade warm, lift the bag interior, keep the liner pure white. Sound: a muffled ACHOO SFX (or her own, low-passed as if heard from inside the bag), a leather thump + key jangle on the jolt, a rustle, a wrapper crinkle on the grip and a whoosh on the exit.
visual_hook_build.lane_and_tool: Owned-phone (recommended): a real phone wedged in a real tan tote, 4K 60fps 0.5x/macro, AE/AF lock, Action mode off, a ~1h shoot in a parked car, ~$0-80 in props (a borrowed bag + a pack of liners), 0 credits. It's more real than AI on every axis that matters here: the jolt physics, the hand-object grab, the phone-grain look, and no logo hallucination. AI start frame + motion (fallback): a Nano Banana Pro 9:16 2k start frame matching frame_1, plus an end frame (hand gripping the liner halfway out of the mouth), animated with Kling 2.x/3.0 start+end frame (a 5s gen, keep the best 2.2s) or Veo 3.1 from the start frame. Expect 4-6 gens. Video models can't fake the relative object bounce of a jolt, so the AI clip is generated still and the jolt is added in the editor, which reads weaker. Either way the editor does the text, the accent shake and the hidden wipe.
visual_hook_build.fallback: If no woman's hand is available: the AI path above (generated with NO shake; the jolt is added in the editor with keyframes + directional blur + a key-jangle SFX). Reject any take showing hand morphing or the liner changing shape. If the grab won't render clean, use the owned-phone plate with NO hand (the jolt + the liner hopping, which anyone can shoot), then go through the hidden wipe into an AI S2 where the hand already holds the liner. That loses the grab but keeps the POV, the jolt and the read.
failure_modes_to_reject: The liner reads as something else: a wet wipe, condom, tea bag, sweet, tampon or winged pad. Use the long flat wrapper and reposition.
The liner is under ~35% of the frame, not in the sharp plane on frame 0, or blurred by the jolt on frame 0.
Frame 0 is dark or murky (an under-exposed bag interior), or the sky clips into the liner edge.
Any brand mark: wrapper print, a car-brand key fob, the Apple logo on the prop phone, a tote logo plaque, the steering-wheel badge in S2.
Clutter: more than two other items, or any white/pastel item (tissue, receipt, lip balm) competing with the liner.
Her face sharp or visibly sneezing in frame (that would need a 'Dramatization' label). Reject the take.
An editor-only shake: the whole frame wobbles but nothing moves inside the bag.
The hand covers the liner before ~1.2s, or long/coloured nails or extra jewellery pull focus.
Any stain, yellowing or used look on the liner, or backlight showing its core.
AI path: extra or fused fingers, the liner morphing during the grab, invented wrapper text, a plastic too-clean CGI look, a camera-shake 'jolt' with no object movement.

shots.angle_or_room: Inside her open tan leather zip-top tote, sitting on her lap in the driver's seat of a parked car (supermarket car park, driver door open). The phone lies at the bottom of the bag looking up at ~45 deg out of the open mouth toward the overcast sky / open door.
shots.what_we_see: FRAME 0: one clean white panty liner in a long, flat, pale-pink unbranded wrapper fills ~40-45% of the frame, dead-centre in the 30-62% height band, tilted ~25 deg, pin-sharp (10-12cm from the lens). Behind it and out of focus: a plain key ring and a phone lying screen-down in a plain case - the only two other items, both dark. Above: the bag mouth is a bright oval of daylight. At most a soft blur of her chin/shoulder at the top edge; her face is never sharp. No stains, no brand marks.
shots.motion_inside_shot: Clip starts 3 frames before the jolt so frame 0 has a sharp liner while the pill pops in. 0.10-0.35 JOLT (in-camera): the bag drops ~4cm and bounces on her lap, the keys slide, the liner hops and resettles in the sharp plane, the daylight in the mouth jumps; editor adds a 3-5 frame accent shake. 0.60-1.30 her right hand (short natural nails, thin gold band) dives in from the top of the mouth, fingers spread, past the blurred keys, straight toward the lens, and pinches the liner by its tab (liner stays >=60% visible until the grip). 1.30-2.05 she yanks it up and out toward the light (motion blur, the mouth flares bright). 2.05-2.20 the back of her hand sweeps across the lens (dark wipe) = hidden cut.
shots.on_screen_text: 0.00 Claret pill, cream text: 'Sneeze. Little pee.' (pops in over frames 0-4, ~18% from top). 1.30 a Warm Cream box stacks UNDER it (line 1 stays): 'Still packing a spare panty liner?'. 1.90 the 🙄 pops onto the end of line 2.
shots.vo_or_dialogue: SFX 0.00-0.20: muffled off-screen 'ACHOO!' (a sound effect; nobody sneezes on camera). Brand VO 0.22-1.20: 'Sneeze. Little pee.' Brand VO 1.30-2.95: 'Still packing a spare panty liner?' [main-cut trim, see vo_fit_issues] (finishes over S2)
shots.sfx: 0.00 muffled ACHOO (low-passed, as if heard from inside the bag); 0.10 leather thump + key jangle on the jolt; 0.70 lining rustle; 1.25 wrapper crinkle on the grip; 1.80 whoosh up and out. Music bed (wry, light plucked) starts low at 0.00.
shots.cut_reason: Hidden cut inside the hand-wipe at 2.20: the back of her hand covers the lens in both clips, so the exit from the bag reads as ONE continuous move. That follows the pacing law (no visible hard cut in 0-3s) and still lands the liner in daylight before the question ends.
shots.tool_rec: Real phone wedged inside a real bag (full build in visual_hook_build): 4K 60fps, 0.5x/macro, AE/AF locked on the liner, Action mode OFF. CapCut keyframed accent shake. Fallback: Nano Banana Pro start frame + Kling 2.x/3.0 start/end frame (or Veo 3.1 from the start frame) with the jolt added in the editor.

shots.angle_or_room: Same car, driver's seat. Phone handheld at her chest height facing the windscreen; plain dash, steering-wheel badge taped over or out of frame, overcast car park soft through the glass.
shots.what_we_see: Her hand holds the wrapped panty liner ~20cm from the lens, centred, long axis vertical, against a softly blurred dashboard and windscreen. Daylight on the wrapper. No face.
shots.motion_inside_shot: 2.20-2.40 the hand pulls back from the lens (the reverse of the wipe) to reveal the liner. 2.55-2.85 her thumb flicks the wrapper tab so it pops half-open and the white liner edge shows (half-peeled in hand is allowed), with a tiny 'see?' waggle on 'liner?'.
shots.on_screen_text: Both hook lines stay up across the wipe: 'Sneeze. Little pee.' / 'Still packing a spare panty liner? 🙄'
shots.vo_or_dialogue: Brand VO: '...spare panty liner?' (ends 2.95)
shots.sfx: 2.20 soft thunk-whoosh out of the wipe; 2.60 wrapper-tab 'tk' crinkle.
shots.cut_reason: Cut on the question mark: the hook is paid off, so hard cut into the liner's day.
shots.tool_rec: Same session, same hand, same car; handheld 4K 60. Fallback: Nano Banana Pro still + Kling 5s, use the best 0.8s.

shots.angle_or_room: Bedroom, morning. Top-down, tripod-locked macro over a cream duvet with soft window light from frame-left.

vo_fit_issues: BEAT 2 (1.30-3.00, 1.7s): the locked 'Still packing a spare liner - for every sneeze?' becomes 9 words with the word-rule 'panty' = 3.75s at 2.4 w/s (3.0s even at the refs' ~3 w/s). PROPOSED TRIM: 'Still packing a spare panty liner?' (6 words). It now mirrors the on-screen line word for word, and 'sneeze' was already spoken at 0.22s. 6 words is still 2.5s at 2.4 w/s, so it needs a brisk ~1.65s read (9 syllables, a normal quick wry question; Everdries #14 reads its 6-word hook question at 3.2 w/s). If ElevenLabs runs long, let it L-cut up to 0.3s into S3 and start the bridge at 3.3s.

BEAT 3 (3.00-11.00, 8s): the locked roast is 33 words = 13.75s at 2.4 w/s (~11s at 3 w/s) and does NOT fit. PROPOSED MAIN-CUT TRIM (22 words, ~7.3s at 3 w/s, ends 10.0s): 'Here's that liner's day. It bunches. It shifts. It feels like a diaper. Another one in the trash. Tomorrow, a new one.' It drops 'the day that little liner actually has' (> 'that liner's day'), 'And by tonight,' (the night-lit bin shot carries it) and 'Same sticker, same routine.' (the zip-close shot carries it). Every CJ attribute stays. Backup if still long: 'Feels like a diaper.' (21 words).

BEAT 4 (11-23, 12s): fits easily (17 words = 7.1s at 2.4 w/s). There is no VO from 18.2s to 23.0s (4.8s), so three moving car-park shots + the music lift + the boot thunk carry it. Nothing sits still.
BEAT 5 (23-30, 7s): 17 words = 7.1s at 2.4 w/s, 5.7s at 3 w/s. It fits at the brisk read, ending 28.2s.

BEAT 6 (end card 30-35, 5s): the locked guarantee is verbatim and can't be trimmed. 17 words = 7.1s at 2.4 w/s / ~5.6s at 3 w/s, longer than the 5s card. FIX: start it at 28.9s under the S20 product beat so it ends ~34.5s on the card. Alternative: a 6s end card (main = 36s).

TOTAL with trims: 82 VO words over ~34.3s = 2.39 w/s average. That passes the 2.4 w/s check overall, with staccato phrases read at ~3 w/s locally (the refs' measured pace: Everdries #14 ~3.2 w/s on the hook, UltraDries #6 2.8-3.5 w/s). Without the trims the locked VO is ~96 words = 40s at 2.4 w/s.
pacing_check.notes: How this beats the refs: the hook reads as ONE continuous move for 3.0s like both refs (Everdries 3.4s, UltraDries 3.0s) but packs 3 motion events (jolt 0.1s, dive 0.6s, yank 1.3s) + the emoji pop, with the only cut hidden inside a hand-wipe. 3-10s has 7 cuts (UltraDries #6: 8; Everdries #14: 2), each a locked macro with a micro-action on its VO word and a new place almost every cut (bed > bed ECU > bathroom > gym bag > night bin > FLASH > hallway > in-bag), plus the 0.4s underwear flash at 8.55s. The reveal (11-23s) runs 7 shots across 3 places (bedroom hands > body > car park), none over 2.3s. Avg shot is 1.67s (vs 2.6s / 5.5s for the refs); the longest live-action hold is 2.6s and only the animated end card holds 5s. LONG CUT (55s): the locked VO verbatim (incl. 'Here's the day that little liner actually has', 'And by tonight', 'Same sticker, same routine', '- for every sneeze?'), + one more liner shot (peeled and binned at the end of the day), + the care beat 'Wash. Hang. Wear again.' (hand rinses and hangs the black underwear, owned-phone), + a second everyday movement (she walks out the front door). Same hook and end card.
